general_information.Description: Air Cargo Management is a practice‑oriented course that equips you with the knowledge and skills to manage the full life cycle of air freight operations. It focuses on how airlines, freight forwarders, ground handlers, and shippers work together to move high‑value cargo safely, quickly, and profitably in today’s global supply chains. Across 11 chapters you will explore industry structure and regulations, the role of IATA cargo agents and forwarders, aircraft and ULD characteristics, airport and terminal facilities, cargo handling processes, booking and acceptance procedures, and the management of special cargo such as perishables and dangerous goods. You will also learn how to calculate air cargo rates and charges, complete and interpret airway bills, and understand the growing importance of cargo digitalization and automation. Throughout the course, real cases and examples will illustrate how air cargo supports trade and logistics development in Vietnam, helping you see clear links between theory and local industry practice. By the end of the module, you will be able to design and evaluate air cargo solutions, communicate effectively with international partners, and position yourself for careers with airlines, 3PLs, e‑commerce logistics providers, and airport operators.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Demonstrate a broad understanding of how the air cargo industry operates within global supply chains.
Interpret and apply fundamental principles of air cargo planning, pricing, and capacity utilization.
Use core documentation and information required for compliant and efficient air cargo movements.
Recognize key safety, security, and regulatory considerations in air cargo operations.
Shows self-reliance when working independently and collaboratively
Demonstrate ethical awareness and reflection in business context

assessments.Question Type: OP1: Divide the class into 4 or 6 groups. Each group will select a global/ Vietnamese air freight carriers and conduct an in-depth analysis of its air freight operations. The report should cover: 1. Company background and industry context 2. Air fleet (types and roles of aircraft used) 3. Main air freight services offered 4. Operational process for handling air cargo 5. Technologies used to streamline operations 6. Common operational issues and company’s solutions to tackle these issues.OP2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal

OP2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal

assessments.Question Type: OP1: Each student writes a 1,500–2,000 words report analyzing one air cargo shipment (real or realistic scenario). The report must include: Shipment overview: route, cargo type, service level, and reason for using air; Key actors: shipper, forwarder, airline, ground handler, customs, and last mile carrier, with brief roles; Process map: step by step flow from booking to final delivery (include a simple diagram); Documents and rules: main documents (e.g. air waybill) and any special handling/regulatory requirements.
